ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-intensity (white) pixels comprise approximately 35-40% of the visible surface area against a primary low-intensity (black) background, characterized by a sharp bimodal distribution.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Extensive distribution of high-contrast white annular rings (rosettes) and irregular circular blobs concentrated heavily in the distal regions and along the trailing margins of both lobes, transitioning to solid low-intensity pixels towards the peduncle junction.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Calculated V-shaped depression with an internal angle of approximately 95 degrees, exhibiting a depth-to-width ratio of 1:2 within the central bounding box.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, high-amplitude pixel variations (serrations) localized along the distal edges, with peak amplitudes of 5-10 pixels relative to the mean edge baseline, often coinciding with rosette clusters.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Concave-to-convex curvature following a sigmoidal path from the median notch to the lateral tips, with the terminal ends showing an upward vertical displacement.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Densely packed constellations of roughly circular white rings (diameter range 5-15 pixels) distributed across 70% of the visible lobe area, consistent with high-contrast barnacle attachment site scarring.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive peripheral calcification or scarring along the trailing edge resulting in a highly irregular, jagged pixel boundary.
